ADMINISTRATIVE
THE CPARTER OF THE BROADC STING CORPORATION OF JAPAN
(Oct. 31, 1945)
CHAPTER I
GENERAL RULES
Article 1. The present Corporation is aimed at operating the
broadcasting industry and radio-telecommunication, as permitted
by the Government and also at developing rodio-telecommnnication.
The orporation may oper te other enterprises connected
with the above object or may invest in those enterprises, which
are necessary for the monagement of the above enterprises.
Article II. The present Corporation shell be styled the Shedan
Hojin Nippon Hoso-Kyokai (Broadcasting Corporation of Japan.,Inc.)
Article III. The Corporation shall have headquarters in Kojimechi
Ward, Tokyo.
Article Iv. Those regulations necessary for the operation of
the present Charter shall be laid down in e by-lew, which shall
be approved by the Board of Directors.
CHAPTER II
MEMBERSHIP
Article V. The members shall each subscribe one share or more to
the funds of the Corporetion, but the heir to a. member who adher-
ed to the Corporation under provisions of Article VI shall be
exempted from the subscription and may be regarded as having

shall apply to the Corporation and obbain the Chairman's approval.
 His membership shall start when he has completed his pay
ment of subscriptions. to the Corporation and when his name is
registered in the list of. members.
Article VII. When a member wishes to withdraw from the Corpo-
ration he shall notify the Corporation to that effect.
When = member violptes the Charter or when his actions,are
regarded as injurious to the prestige of the Corporation, his
name may be stricken from the list of members.
CHAPTER III
OFFICIALS
Article vIII. The Corporation shall have Directors.. not exceea-
ing 25 in number and Superintendents not exceeding 3 in number.
Both the Lirectors and. Superintendents shall be members
ofthe Corporation.
On the decision of a general meeting of members, the Cor-
poration may nominate one President end one Vice-President and
several advisers.
Article IX. The Directors and Superintendents shall be elected
by the meeting..of..Councillors.

Article X. The Directors shall mutually elect one Chairman, one
Managing Director, and three Executive Directors.
Article XI. Deleted.
'rticle XII. The Directors shall organize a Board of Directors

Article XIv. The Menaging Director shall assist the Chairman
and supervise routine business. In case the Chairman is pre-
vented from attending to business by unavoidable circumstances,
the Managing Director shall act for him.
Article Xv. The Executive Directors shall take charge of those
affairs designated by the Chairman, and in case the Managing
Director is prevented from attending to business by unavoidable
circumstances shall act for him under his direction.
Article XVI. The term of office for the Directors and Super-
intendents shall be each a full three years, but they shall
remain in office even after the expiration of their term until

CHAPTER IV
GENERAL MEETING
Article XIX. A regular general meeting of members shall be held
once a year, within three months of the end of every financial
year, and an extraordinary general meeting of members shall be
held from time to time on the decision of the Board of Directors
with the exception of those provided for by the Civil Codes.
frticle XX. The members shall each have one vote at a general
meeting per share of subscription. Voting at a general meeting
shall not be done except by the principal or his proxy, who must
Irticle XXI. The resolutions before a general meeting shall be
decided by a majority vote of the members in attendence, and in
case of tie, the vote of the Chairman shall be decisive. But
a resolution concerning a modification or amendment of the Char-
ter shall be decided by a more than three-quarters majority vote
of the members in attendance.
Article XXII. Deleted.

CHAPTER V
ASSETS AND ACCOUNTING
Article XXIII. The assets of the Corporetion shall consist of
contributions, subscriptions, listening fees, miscelleneous
revenue, and other assets.
Article XXIv. The financial year of the Corporation shall begin
on 'pril 1 of every year and end on March 31 of the next yeer.
Article XXv. The Corporation's settlement of accounts shall be
submitted to the regular genernl meeting of members every year
for approvel.
Article XXVI. A member shall not meke eny claim on the Corpora-
tion's assets even if he withdraws or is expelled from the
Corporation.
In case, however, the Board of Directors decides otherwise,
the provision shall not be applicable within the extent of his
subscription to tre Corportion's fund.
Article XXVII. In case the Corporatios is cissolved end in cese
there is any residue of estate, it shall be distributed among the
members in proportion to their subscriptions to the Corporation's
fund.

Article I. The budget and settlement of accounts of the Corpo-
ration shall be approved by the Board of Directors.
Article II. Those borrowings which will not be repaid during
the operation of an enterprise in connection with which they
will be made, as well as those borrowings which will be made.
for promoting a new enterprise, shall be approved by the Board .
of Directors.
Article III. The Chairman of the Board of Directors may set
up a committee, if it is deemed necessary, to serve as an advi-
sory body for him with regard to the broadcasting industry.
Article IV. The Chairman shall lay down regulptions for con-
trol of the organization of the Corporation, staff members,
and business, as well as conduct of affairs releting to the
Corporation.
Article V. The Superintendent who attends to routine business
shall be one in number and the said Superintendent shall be
mutually elected by the Superintendents.
Article VI. Those who attend to the Corporation's business,
receiving fixed pay as its staff members, shall not be eligible
for the allowances stipulated in Article XVII Paragraph 2.

Article VII... Those matters stipulated in the Charter and its
By-Law, as well as those deemed important: by the Chairman of
the Board of Directors, shall be referred to the Board of Direc-
tors.
Article VIII. The decisions of the Board of Directors shall be
token by a majority vote of tre directors in attendance and. in
case of tie, the vote cast by the Chairman shall be decisive.
Article IX. With the exception of those matters, to discuss
which a general regular meeting of members shall be convoked,
the Chairman of the Board of Directors may seek the views of
directors by letter for the sake of expediency on matters which
must be referred to the Board of Directors, and substitute the
Board of Directors' decision by putting them to a vote in acéoř-
dence with the provisions in the foregoing erticle. Put the
decisions taken in this manner shall be communicated to all the
Directors or reported to the next meeting of the Board of Direc-
tors, together with the circumstonces leading to the decision
taken.
Article X. The Creirman of the Boerd of Directors may act et
his discretion on those matters which otherwise must be referred
to the Board of Directors end which fell under either of the
following parapraphs. But this provision shall not be appli-
cable to those matters which must be referred to the general
meeting of members..
1. Those matters which require urgent attention, so that

there is no time for calling a meeting of the Board of Directors
or taking decision in accordance with the foregcing Article.
2. Those matters which are easy or for dealing with which

been decided by the Chairmen at his discretion in accordance with
the above-mentioned provision shall be reported to the next meet-

Article XI. Those matters, which have been decided by the Board
of Directors shall be recorded and signed by more than two Direc-
tors who have attended the meeting.
Article XII. The Superintendents may attend a meeting of the
Board of Directors and express their views.
Article XIII. The Superintendent who attends to routine business
may convoke a meeting of Superintendents on approval of the Chair-
man of the Board of Directors.
The Provisions of Articles VIII to X inclusive shall be
applied to the meeting of Superintendents.
Article XIv. The Chairman of the Board of Directors shall call
a meeting of Councillors.
The Chairman of the meeting of Councillors shall be elected
by those Councillcrs in attendance. The provisions of Article
VIII shall be applied to the meeting of Councillors.

Brief  iographical Jotes on presidents of BCJ
Kenzo Iwahara: Born in October, the 3rd year of Bunkyu (1863)
Formerly President and Director of the Japan Wireless
Telegraphic Company, and occupied the post of director in various
other companies successively.
In December, the 13th year of Taisho (1924), was elected
Chief Commissioner of Tokyo Broadcasting Station.
In August, the 15th year of Taisho (1926), was installed as
President of the Broadc sting Corporation of Japan, and continued
until his death in July, the 11th year of Showa (1926).
Shichiro Komori: Born in October, the 6th year of Meiji (1873)
In July, t e 35th year of eiji (1902), graduated after
completing the course of law, from the Tokyo Imperial University.
In January, the 36th year of Leiji (1903), entered the
service of the …inistry of Communications, and occupied the
post of Chief in tre apporo, Tokyo, and Osaka Bureaus of Commu-
nications successively, efter which he was elected Chief Commis-
sioner of the Marine Court of Inquiry (Kai In Shimban Shocho)
for tre Osaka district.
In August, the 15th year of Taisho (1925), was elected to
the post of managing Director of Broadcesting Corporation of
Japan, and then promoted to the post of Executive Director.
In eptember, the 11th year of Showa (1936), became presi-
dent of BCJ, and resigned in May, the 15th year of Showa (1943).
- 2 -

=== Page 14 === (confidence 0.98)
RI-114-RA-B-2
Hiroshi Shimomura: Born in May, the 8th year of Me1ji (1875).
In July, the 31st year of Meiji (1898), greduated from the
Department of Politics of the Tokyo Imperial University. Immedi-
ately entered The Ministry of Communications. After serving there
as Director of the Pureau of Postal Savings and then as Director
of the Bureau of Postal Money Ord-rs and Savings, he was trans-
ferred to the post of Chief irector of Ceneral iffairs in the
Covernment-General of Formosa. Meanwhile he had received tre
degree of Doctor of Law.
In September, the 10th year of Taisho (1921), joined the
Tokyo daily newspeper "Asahi Shimbun", becoming Executive Direc-
tor in May, the 11th year of Taisho (1922), and Vice-President in
February, the 5th year of Show? (1930), holding the two positions
concurrently. Resigned from these posts in Merch, the 1lth year
of Showa (1936).
In January, the 12th year of Showa (1937), was appointed
by the Emperor a member of the House of Peers.
In May, the 18th year of Showe (1943), was appointed Presi-
dent of the Broadcasting Corporation of Japan. Resigned from
this post in April, 1945.
On April 7th, the 20tr year of Showa (1945), he was con-
currently appointed Minister of State and Director of the Infor-
mation ureau in Premier Suzuki's Cabinet.
On August 15th, the 20th year of Showa (1945), he was eppoin-
ted an 'dvisor to the Ministry of Welfare.
At present Mr. Hiroshi Shimomura is in the custody of the
Allied War Crimes Commission at Sugamo Prison.

=== Page 15 === (confidence 0.99)
RI-114-RA-B-2
Hachiro Ohashi: Born in December, the 18th year of e1ji (1885)
In July, the 43rd year of Meiji (1910), finished the course
of politics at Tokyo Imperial University. Immediately after
graduation he entered the service of the Ministry of Communice-
tions, and successively occupied the posts of Chief of the Postal
Affairs Bureau, Bureau of Accounting, and of Vice-Linister, final-
ly to be transferred to the position of Director-General of the
Bureau of Legislature and then become Secretary-in-Chief in Premier
Okada's Cabinet.
In November, the 12th year of Show (1937), was appointed
successively Director and President of the Japan Wireless Tele-
greph Company, resigning from it in March of the following year
(meanwhile the name of that company had been changed to "Inter-
national Telecommunications Company"). In the same year was
elected Commissioner of the Japan Radio Broadcasting Corporetion.
In May, the 20th year of Showa (1945), was appointed Pre-
sident of the aforementioned company, and later held the post
of Councillor for the Bureau of Information.
On Feb. 20th, the 21st yerr of Showa (1946), he resigned from
the Presidency of BCJ by order of SCAP (see Apnendix #1).

THE BROADCASTING CORPORATION OF JAPAN
21 February, 1946
Resignation of the President.
We hereby report thet the President of the Broadcasting
Corporation of Japn, Hachiro Ohashi, who had previously expressed
his intention of resigning from his position, has formelly resig-
ned on the 20th inst. upon the acceptance of his resignation by
the meeting of the Board of Directors.
flenceforth, until such time as the new President shall have
been selected, the trree directors shall act as deputy execu-
tives and conduct the Corporation business through mutual con-
sultations.
In the relationships of the Corporation with outside parties,
the Permanent Director, Kenjiro Yabe, shall act as the representa-
tive.
Board of Directors
The Broadcesting Corporation of Japan

Note: 1. Standard frequency accuracy, 3 parts in 10,000,000.
2. Ordinary time system (60 pulses per minute). 59th pulse not transmitted. Accuracy 0.03 second.
3. Rhythmic time system (61 pulses per minute). 1st pulse of each minute is 1/2 second dash.

minute, "D" in the second minute and "B" in the 3rd minute.
5. Source of standard frequency: MOTC Standard Frequency Station, Makuhari, Chiba.Prefecture.

SUBJECT:
Radio Interference Experienced by Aircraft
Control Tower Frequency in Japan.
OLY
EUR
FCC
894.76/12-2449
The Ambassador has the honor to refer to the
Department's telegram no. 724 of October 4, 1949,
respecting interference by a radio station in North
Korea on the 4495 kilocycle aircraft control tower
frequency in Japan on which the United States has
prior registration dated October 27, 1938.
By note, nc. 577 dated Cctober 4, 1949, the
Embassy brought this matter to the attention of the
Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs, forwarding a
copy of that note to the Department under cover of
despatch no. 565, Cctober 4, 1949. The reply, con-
tained in note no. 83 of December 15, 1949, confines
itself to pointing out that the interfering station
"is not located within the territory of the Soviet
Union".
A summary of the Ministry's note no. 83 has
been transmitted to the Department by the Embassy
telegram no. 3176 of today's date.
JAN 161950

=== Page 1045 === (confidence 0.99)
Translation
Ministry.of Foreign
Affairs of the USSR
No. 83
The Minis try of Foreign Affairs of the Union
of Soviet Socialist Republics presents its compliments
to the Ambassador of the United States of America
and with reference to Embassy's note no. 577 of
Cctober 4, 1949 in which the Soviet Government is
urgently requested "to render assistance" in with-
drawing radio interference allegedly originating
from a station at Hanhyn, Northern Korea, has the
honor to state that the Soviet Government is not
able to fulfill your reguest since interference at
4495 kilocycle frequency is created, as you indicated,
at a radio station which is not located within the
territory of the Soviet Union.
Moscow, December 15, 1949
To the Embassy
of the United States of America,
Moscow.
Seal no. l of the
Ministry of Foreign
Affairs of the USSR,
